newsitem.title: BELGIUM: TRACTEBEL TO ISSUE 46 BLN BFR STOCK WITHOUT PUT.
newsitem.headline: TRACTEBEL TO ISSUE 46 BLN BFR STOCK WITHOUT PUT.

text.p: Belgian utility holding company Tractebel SA said on Wednesday that it would issue about three million new shares without a put warrant as part of the agreed merger with its Powerfin unit.
At current market prices the issue is worth some 46 billion Belgian francs.

At the moment all free-floating Tractebel shares have a put warrant which allows holders to sell the stock at a guaranteed 14,500 francs to Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) within three years.

"This way Tractebel will definitively remain bourse-listed since the new shares issued for this merger will not have a put warrant," Tractebel chief executive officer Philippe Bodson said in a speech at the annual general meeting.

Afterwards he told Reuters that if for some reason stock markets would crash and Tractebel shares would fall below 14,500 francs the share would disappear from the bourse since all minority shareholders would sell to SGB.
SGB owns 64.22 percent in Tractebel following the purchase of a large block from Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA (GBL) last year.
As part of the deal with GBL and to avoid a full bid for all Tractebel stock, SGB gave minority shareholders the put warrant.
After the Tractebel/Powerfin merger, on which shareholders of both groups will vote on Thursday, SGB's Tractebel stake will fall to 50.27 percent.
As part of the merger the three million new Tractebel shares will be exchanged for nine million Powerfin shares not owned by Tractebel at a three for one ratio.
Full details of the swap will be given in the prospectus on the share issue due out later on Wednesday.
